svg.title: Data-flow diagram — LEVEL 0 (context) and LEVEL 1 (decomposition), with trust boundaries

g.text: Data-flow diagram — LEVEL 0 (context) and LEVEL 1 (decomposition), with trust boundaries
Every flow that carries Salesforce CRM or personal data is tagged
· processes, data stores and the three trust boundaries
Every published port binds 0.0.0.0. Nothing inside authenticates the caller.
:3000 frontend · :8080 orchestrator · :8000 vllm · :8001 vllm-vision · :8002 vllm-router · :8003 vllm-embed
docker-compose.yml:86,133,171,202,272-273,351-352 — no `networks:` block, so every container reaches every other
TRUST BOUNDARY 2 — UNTRUSTED CONTENT → MODEL PROMPT
Web pages, pasted URLs, cloned GitHub repos and uploaded archives cross here.
Content is fenced and system blocks folded first (llm.py:39-69); uploads are profiled, never executed (config.py:169).
There is no instruction-stripping, no provenance tainting and no output-side egress check.
Everything inside holds a local replica of production Salesforce data.
DuckDB is opened read_only=True with enable_external_access=False (engines/sql.py:124-132) —
that lockdown, not sql_guard, is what actually contains a prompt-injected query.
TB1 · the boundary that is not enforced.
`auth.py:95-97` `require_user()` returns the single local user and
`/chat` and `/reports*` are deliberately auth-free. That is only safe
if the ports are private — but `docker-compose.yml:272-273` is
Flows F1, F4, F5, F6 all cross TB1 unauthenticated.
and `main.py:343` only 404s `if conv_owner is not None`. A SQLite
asserts the opposite. Flow F2 is the affected hop.
caps neither `messages` nor the base64 `image`/`pdf` strings, and
`main.py:47-53` installs CORS as the only middleware — Starlette adds
retains every token frame for the generation's whole life.
hand-written scanner, not a parser: the checks run on `bare` but the
string that executes is `cleaned` (`sql_guard.py:156`), and an
`E'\''` escape-string desynchronises the two — a reproduced bypass
smuggles `; ATTACH` past both the stacked-statement check
What actually holds the line is `engines/sql.py:124-132`:
inside `async def`** — one slow query stalls every user's SSE stream.
user-influenced URL is fetched: scheme allowlist (`:94-95`), DNS
each of ≤3 redirect hops re-validated (`:147`), time and size capped.
Residual gaps — the validated IP is discarded at `net.py:99` and httpx
`100.64.0.0/10` (CGNAT / Tailscale) is not blocked; there is no
total deadline and `socket.getaddrinfo` (`:76`) has no timeout.
in the repo — magic-byte sniffing, never `extractall()`, zip-slip
(`:153-156`, `:251-253`), four bomb caps plus a live streaming budget
(`:200-208`). Two residual gaps: extraction is **synchronous inside a
archive runs on the event loop; and the byte budget is
(`archive.py:216`), so N concurrent uploads each get 2048 MB.
`<workspace_dir>/uploads` as one entry, so a single TTL expiry
deletes every conversation's extracted uploads at once.
The RS256 signing key is written to
`data` volume** that is mounted read-write into the orchestrator
(`docker-compose.yml:269`) and holds the warehouse the LLM queries.
The JWT itself carries no `iat`/`nbf` and no skew allowance
A RAG-indexing failure is swallowed at `syncworker/main.py:174-184`
while the watermark still advances at `:188` — a **permanent
index gap**. Salesforce deletes are never propagated
16 DDL statements plus a full-table de-dup `DELETE` (`:181-186`) on
DuckDB per-object tables have no PRIMARY KEY or index
(`syncworker/storage.py:140`), so every upsert `DELETE … WHERE Id IN`
`..`, separators, absolute paths, dotfiles, NUL and symlink escape
(`:31-47`), but there is **no extension allowlist and no
rows (`engines/sql.py:407-409`), so anyone who can reach :8080 can
enumerate and download every export any analyst has ever produced.
all on one DGX Spark host
